chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir quoted on the authority of Al-Mo'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Zurara ibn A'yun that he had heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:
We are twelve Imams, among them Al-Hasan and Al-Hussein, and then the Imams are from the descendants of Al-Hussein (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (referring to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith regarding the number of Imams in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) explicitly identifies the twelve Imams as descending from the lineage of Husayn (AS), reinforcing the Twelver doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and divine appointment (*Nass*). It serves as a critical proof text for the continuity of leadership from the Prophet's household, distinguishing the specific twelve from other branches of the family. This narration underscores the theological certainty of the Imamate's number and lineage, central to Shia creedal identity.
